title: stale_at_check.sh silently excludes live threads with no acceptance.md, and its skip line reads as complete
body:
**`stale_at_check.sh` walks `intent/st/*/acceptance.md`, and a live thread with no `acceptance.md` on disk is excluded from BOTH the numerator and the announced skip list.**

Measured 2026-08-30 (vc) at `3d76f156`, store versus tool:

    tool output:  "examined 37 to-write row(s) with a citation, of 266 AT row(s)
                   (skipped 1 not-started/cancelled thread(s): ST0046(not-started))"

    store:        386 AT rows across 69 threads
                  62 to-write rows carry a citation: ST0056 37, ST0060 16, ST0046 9

The tool's 266 is exactly the five live threads that have an `acceptance.md` on disk (ST0055 16 + ST0056 165 + ST0057 69 + ST0061 7 + ST0068 9). **ELEVEN live threads carrying 111 AT rows between them have no `acceptance.md`** -- ST0043, ST0044, ST0045, ST0047, ST0048, ST0050, ST0051, ST0052, ST0053, ST0054, ST0060, ST0067 -- and the tool names none of them.

**THE SKIP LINE IS WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A LIMIT.** It reports one skipped thread by name and reason, which reads as a complete account of what was not examined. ST0060's 16 to-write-with-citation rows are neither examined nor named, and its status is `triage`, so it does not qualify for the declared not-started/cancelled skip either. **A denominator that reads as the estate is 69% of it.**

`inert_arg_check.sh`, a sibling instrument in the same directory, states the rule this one breaks: *"A ROW THE FIXTURE CANNOT DRIVE IS DECLARED UNDRIVABLE WITH ITS REASON, never skipped: a skipped row is indistinguishable from a clean one."*

**AND THE POPULATION SOURCE IS A RENDERING.** D01 makes the SQLite store SSOT; `acceptance.md` is a generated view and `intent/.canon/st/*.json` is the committed extract. The tool reads both and never the store, so it inherits every lag either of them has. The fix is one query against `tests`, which also removes the on-disk-view dependency that causes the exclusion.

**COST TODAY: NONE IN THE CUT.** ST0056/ST0058/ST0066/ST0068 all have an `acceptance.md`, and of the invisible threads only ST0060 (out of the cut) carries rows in the class this tool hunts. The tool's finding for the cut is correct and complete. **This is a post-tag fix, filed so the blind spot is recorded rather than rediscovered** -- if ST0056's view were ever absent or renamed, the same silence would apply to the cut and the tool would still print a clean report.

**WHAT THE TOOL GOT RIGHT, AND IT OUTPERFORMED THE CENSUS THAT FOUND THIS.** vc's own ad-hoc store census returned 11 stale rows; the tool returns 2. The nine-row difference is ST0046, which the tool correctly excludes as not-started and the census counted. **The instrument in the tree was more accurate than the one written to check it.**
